product.heading: What is EduGame Studio?
product.description: A Windows desktop app that turns lesson plans and teaching materials into games your class can play — even without internet.
points: Reads lesson plans from DOCX, PDF, PPTX, TXT or MD files, or pasted text
Five ready-made game types with fullscreen play and 3D visuals
Local AI on llama.cpp — no account needed, your lesson never leaves the machine
Games and history stored in SQLite, exported as .egame files you can move by USB
Presents to a second screen and lets students answer on their phones over LAN

games.heading: Game showcase
games.description: The five game types currently available in EduGame Studio. Easy to add more later.

items.title: Knowledge Arena
items.description: Multiple-choice questions with right/wrong feedback and explanations. Five scoring modes: basic, speed, by difficulty, team battle (2–6 teams) and practice; fullscreen play adds the House Building mode.

items.title: Scenario Challenge
items.description: A branching story where each choice has consequences and affects later situations. Scored on decision quality or simple right/wrong, with discussion questions.

items.title: Knowledge Matching
items.description: Four ways to play: two-column matching, memory flip cards, categorising, and “Knowledge Constellation” — a 3D star board where students drag answer cards onto the right star.

items.title: Treasure Hunt
items.description: A multi-stage journey: puzzles, missions and a final challenge, with a progress map, hints after wrong answers, branch choices and several endings.

items.title: Learning Race
items.description: Teams take turns answering to advance on a race track: easy +1, medium +2, hard +3, plus boost, lucky and challenge cells, alongside knowledge points.

items.title: Five-step game creation
items.description: Guided steps from a raw lesson plan to a drafted game; switch game type without regenerating the content.

items.title: AI on your own machine
items.description: llama.cpp with Qwen3.5 2B or 4B, downloaded automatically, verified by SHA-256 and bound to 127.0.0.1 — lesson text never leaves the computer.

items.title: Built for the whole class
items.description: Fullscreen gameplay, output to a second screen, team battles, and students answering on their phones over the LAN.

items.title: Author questions your way
items.description: Write them yourself, import CSV/XLSX, paste text (seven question types, duplicate detection) or let AI draft them — locally or in the cloud.

items.title: Offline-first
items.description: Creating, playing, scoring and reviewing history all work without a connection; games live in SQLite and export to .egame.

items.title: Your personal teaching style
items.description: Tone, humour, art preferences and favourite examples are stored per teacher and used as AI defaults when generating questions.

download.heading: Download
download.requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit (x64) — no ARM64 build yet. The installer is 88.2 MB, installs per user and needs no administrator rights. For local AI: 4 GB RAM minimum for the 2B model or 8 GB for the 4B model, plus a few GB of free disk (Qwen3.5-2B ~1.2 GB + runtime ~19 MB). The app has no code-signing certificate, so SmartScreen will warn — choose More info → Run anyway after verifying the SHA-256: 636bc0042611516987c3fbfc48c61f1d65df0935ab5a17f31fb39fb80fe81741.
download.releaseNotes: 0.4.1 (Nov 5, 2026): new brand identity (graduation-owl mascot, per-genre game card colours, Title Case labels); pure-CSS animations plus offline confetti; dark mode gains surface elevation tiers and a fix for help boxes that were nearly unreadable; type back at the 11 px floor; wizard drops ALLCAPS. The build passes 87/87 unit tests and 11/11 packaged-binary checks. Not code-signed and never yet installed on an offline clean machine. Full notes are on the v0.4.1 GitHub release page.
download.trial: There is no separate trial build — the full installer is described above.
